subject: EchoVance: proposal for dedicated standby on-call & availability corridor
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Cheng <olivia@echovance.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@echovance.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EchoVance request: dedicated standby on-call + availability corridor

Hi team — looping you in on a request from EchoVance (attached SOW + runbook draft). They are asking for a tailored availability corridor and a dedicated standby on-call/resource lane for their pilot. Key asks from the customer: 

- P95 generation latency commitment: sub-50ms for their realtime inference path (payloads ~200 tokens).
- Dedicated standby on-call (Redwood SRE rotation) during peak hours and immediate pager coverage during incidents affecting EchoVance's production region (us-west).
- A fallback routing policy that preserves correctness but allows temporary model variant fallback if dedicated pool is degraded (they want rollback safety and clear escalation).
- Operational access: read-only runbook and runbook-review sessions; weekly sync during pilot.
- Financial ask: limited service credit if we miss the agreed availability or response-floor during the 6-week pilot.

They're proposing a 6-week pilot with anticipated QPS of ~80 at 95th percentile spikes (bursty windows up to 400 qps for short bursts). This is a strategic account for us — pilot likely converts if we can demonstrate the corridor and ops support.

Can SRE/product confirm feasibility and what product work (if any) is required to formalize a 'standby on-call' offering and the technical constraints around sub-50ms p95? Also need an initial ops cost estimate for the standby rotation (people-hours + runbook maintenance) and guidance on whether Dedicated capacity + routing policy is the right approach vs hosted with warm standby.

Attachments: EchoVance_SOW_v1.pdf, echovance-runbook-draft.md

Next steps I propose: SRE + Product quick feasibility call today (30m) and an internal ops cost sanity check. I can pull finance/legal in after we have a technical feasibility note.

Thanks —
Tessa
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Cheng <olivia@echovance.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EchoVance request: dedicated standby on-call + availability corridor

Tessa — thanks for the context and attachments. Quick initial thoughts from SRE side:

1) Sub-50ms p95 is achievable under controlled conditions (short sequences, optimized model variant, local GPU pool). But it depends on model choice, quantization, and whether we accept smaller batch sizes (cost increases).
2) Traffic profile questions I need answered before costing:
   - What is the actual percentile distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99) and token length histogram?
   - How long are the "bursty windows" (seconds, minutes)?
   - What percentage of requests need the strict corridor vs those that can tolerate fallback?
3) Dedicated standby on-call: we can run a rotational standby (2 people/shift) but it will require a formal on-call SOW: on-call rota, escalation matrix, incident response SLA, and compensation for dedicated coverage. Estimate: ~0.4 FTE sustained (with spike coverage paid as overtime) during pilot. Will produce a draft ops cost estimate after you confirm profile answers above.
4) Fallback model routing: we recommend a pre-approved compatible model variant (e.g., gpt-*-q4f16) that preserves behaviour within an acceptable regression delta. We'll need to run a short eval set to validate.

I'll volunteer to lead the ops cost note and runbook adjustments. Can we get the traffic histogram from EchoVance (Samir/Olivia)? Also, flagging a dependency: product work for "dedicated standby" signaling in the console — we need a small API/flag to mark requests as high-priority and surface them to dedicated pool.

Marcus
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Cheng <olivia@echovance.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@echovance.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EchoVance request: dedicated standby on-call + availability corridor

Thanks — really helpful summary. Product feasibility notes: 

- Short term (pilot-friendly): we can implement an operational routing policy using existing Dedicated capacity with an explicit "priority-traffic" tag. That avoids the need for an immediate runtime change. The tag will ensure requests route to the reserved pool; SRE can handle rota. No server-side code changes required, just configuration and console UI visibility (we can script the tagging via API). Delivery: ~1 sprint (2 weeks) to make the console filters clearer and add admin flags.

- Medium term: to make this repeatable product feature (self-serve standby on-call + routing), we should schedule a small feature to support an internal "standby on-call" offering: admin UI for standby, billing line item, and incident handoff tooling. I estimate 3 sprints (6 weeks) of focused work if prioritized.

- Latency: achieving sub-50ms p95 will require: a tuned model variant, pre-warmed KV caches, and reserve GPU memory to avoid cold starts. We can meet the perf target in Dedicated with enforced batch-size caps and continuous warmup (extra cost). We should quantify the incremental cost to EchoVance and whether they accept the fallback policy as a safety valve.

Operational asks from Product for pilot: 
1) Answer Marcus' traffic histogram questions.
2) Signed pilot SOW with clear success criteria (p95 target, incident credit thresholds).
3) Commitment window for feature work if EchoVance converts (do they expect self-serve within 3 months?).

Priyom — can you flag any commercial considerations (credit sizing, pilot pricing) we should propose for the SOW? If finance wants a conservative credit cap, we should suggest a tiered credit scheme tied to duration of outage and impact.

Monica
Group PM, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: EchoVance request: dedicated standby on-call + availability corridor

Thanks for the quick responses — summary and proposed next steps: 

Summary:
- SRE: sub-50ms p95 feasible in Dedicated with quantization + warm pools; ops cost approx 0.4 FTE sustained for pilot (Marcus to confirm after histogram).
- Product: short-term config-based routing + admin visibility (1 sprint); full self-serve standby offering requires 3 sprints.
- Commercial: Priyom to propose pilot pricing + credit scheme (tiered).

Action items: 
- EchoVance (Samir): please share token-length histogram and p95/p99 traffic percentiles. (Samir — flagged in CC)
- Marcus: draft ops cost note + SOW language for on-call (target EOD Mon 7/22).
- Monica: confirm UI config scope and timeline; draft minimal console admin checklist.
- Priyom: suggested pilot pricing and credit cap by Tue 7/23.
- Tessa: I'll schedule a 30m internal sync tomorrow to confirm the go/no-go and then a joint call with EchoVance Friday to close SOW items if feasible.

If Marcus/Monica confirm technical feasibility with the traffic hist, I'll loop Legal for a light SLA addendum. Rajiv — including you for visibility on any exec-level approvals if we have to commit to standby.

—
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
